result.reason: Clarity: A signposts its three commentary items explicitly, glosses jargon in plain English ("the extra yield these bonds offered over safer bonds" vs. B's unexplained "credit spreads"), states the measurement basis (time-weighted, before unitrust payments), and explains the purpose of the cash build. B refers to pre-funding "upcoming distributions" before it has explained the distribution at all, and packs two unrelated portfolio moves into one dense paragraph. Tone: the tone notes call for formality, addressing the trustee as Mrs. Delacourt, full trust name, and a cc to Mr. Ambrose. A delivers all of that plus letterhead, date, and account reference; B drops the letterhead, date, and cc, and jointly addresses trustee and income beneficiary, blurring the fiduciary distinction. B also slips into retail-marketing register ("your portfolio," "We successfully executed our plan," "your continued trust in our partnership," and a closing commitment to "providing steady income and preserving capital"), which is over-familiar for a nine-year formal relationship and faintly promissory. Neither letter leaks the internal retention concern. Lengths are comparable, so the preference is not a length effect.
